newsitem.title: UK: CWC forced to cut investment plans - paper.
newsitem.headline: CWC forced to cut investment plans - paper.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Communications Plc (CWC), the British cable telephone and television group, has been forced to cut its investment plans after failing to hit profit targets, The Independent reported on Wednesday.
The report said the cuts were ordered by telephone group Cable & Wireless Plc, which owns more than 50 percent of a company formed earlier this year in a four-way merger.

It said the setback emerged in figures for trading for the three months to the end of June supplied by CWC to its parent company. The company will not report its maiden results for the six months to end-September until the autumn.
The cuts would reduce spending on the roll-out of cable infrastucture to homes and could also hit CWC's plans to launch 200-channel digital television services later this year, the report said.
CWC was formed by the merger of the Mercury unit of Cable & Wireless with the British cable units of NYNEX Cable Comms Bell Cablemedia Plc and Videotron.
